analysis: Both changed files are test-only: NativeBlockRetirementBridgeTests.swift (adds a TextSession fixture at head lines 50-71 and the test nativeBlockRequestsCarryNoStopScope at lines 95-117) and the new ReasoningStopScopeTests.swift (pure unit tests of ReasoningStopScope.scope and StopHoldback). No production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache storage or fan-helper path is modified, so there is no direct change to the A-001..A-019 assets or the TB-002/TB-007/TB-011 boundaries. The tests use in-memory fixtures with a fake tokenizer and a fake session. They touch no real keys, network, files or secrets. Security-adjacent behavior they pin: stop-sequence scoping for reasoning/tool-call segments (Qwen/DeepSeek think, Gemma4 channel) and that the native block engine ignores the scope and reports the matched stop. This concerns output-truncation semantics, not confidentiality or integrity. The tests refer to production symbols (ReasoningStopScope, CBv2StopStringScope, StopHoldback, EngineV2RequestUsageSignal, the stopStringScope parameter of submitTokenized) whose implementation is outside this supplied batch. The corresponding source changes in other batches should be checked for correct stop handling. In particular, scoped matching must not let a scope bypass hide stop strings or tool-call content in a way that leaks reasoning to consumers beyond existing behavior. The tests assert that reasoning text is still emitted in the output, which appears to be existing behavior. No threat-model update is needed from these test-only units.
